title: Book: Good Strategy/Bad Strategy
summary: Review of Rumelt's Good Strategy/Bad Strategy, emphasizing the distinction between genuine strategy (focused on proximate objectives grounded in reality) and bad strategy (ambition without choice or acknowledgment of challenges). Key concepts include the necessity of choice under scarcity, the leader's duty to reduce ambiguity for teams, and the context-dependence of strategic approaches.
when-to-read: Read this when you need to distinguish between genuine strategic planning and vague aspirational goal-setting, or when you're trying to help teams understand what makes a strategy actionable. Avoid confusing this with books on leadership style or charisma; this article emphasizes that effective strategy is independent of a leader's personal charisma and focuses instead on realistic problem-solving and forcing difficult choices.
